name: Prone Incline Cobra Y-Raise
description: The prone incline cobra Y-raise combines a thoracic extension (cobra) with an overhead Y-arm position, training the lower trapezius and serratus anterior in the overhead range while also loading the thoracic extensors. The Y-arm position (arms raised diagonally overhead at 45 degrees from the spine) targets the lower trapezius more specifically than T or W positions, as the lower trap is primarily responsible for upward scapular rotation and depression when the arms are elevated.

execution.starting_position: Lie prone on an incline bench (15-30 degrees). Arms hang in front. Thumbs pointing up.
execution.setup_instructions: No load or very light dumbbells (1-3 kg). Focus is on motor control, not strength.
steps: Step 2: Extend the thoracic spine (cobra movement) simultaneously while raising the arms in a Y shape — 45 degrees from the spine.
Step 3: At the top, the arms form a Y overhead, thumbs pointing upward.
Step 5: Lower both the arms and the thoracic extension simultaneously.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise. Inhale lowering.
common_mistakes: Arms going too wide (T position) or too narrow — the Y angle is 45 degrees
Extending from the lumbar spine — the thoracic spine is what should move
safety_considerations: Bodyweight or very light load only — this is a postural exercise
No pain should occur during this exercise — stop if any shoulder discomfort arises
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hang to Y position with thoracic extension.
coaching_cues: Thumbs point to the ceiling at the top
Y shape — not T, not overhead — 45 degrees
Lead with the chest for the thoracic extension
